frontier.hypothesis: x3 holds all four target seats with the D stores in place, so the only thing between it and a match is that sched1 hoists the &D_800A35D0 lui/addiu/addu triple to the top of blk=1. A body that keeps the group-A pointer single-death while leaving a real dependence that pins that triple below the group-A stores is a very-low-score body.
frontier.mechanism: In the floor body the shared `ptr` pseudo serialises the group-A, group-D and group-C pointer computations, and that anti-dependence is what holds the D address at rows 49/50/51. Splitting the group-A pointer out (required for local-alloc.c:471-472 to give it a quantity) removes the edge, and sched.c's list scheduler then has no predecessor for the lui/addiu pair.
frontier.next_probe: Dump blk=1 of x3 (tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s36/v/x3.c, `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_800770B8` then read the .sched) and run tools/sched_solver on it: enumerate the schedules in which the D-address triple sits at the target's slots with every other insn unmoved, and ask which C-level dependence would force that. Candidates to spell: the group-D pointer sharing a local with the group-C pointer only; the group-A local declared inside a tighter scope; the group-D address taken from a local that the group-A stores must write first through a genuine read. If sched_solver returns FORECLOSED for the target slot with a single-death group-A pointer present, bank that as the predicate that closes the conflict route and leaves the refs route (item 2) as the only one.

frontier.hypothesis: On the w3 chassis the reload is its OWN quantity (b48 d52 refs4, qty_compare_1 priority 2*4/4 = 2.0). Raising it to refs >= 8 at the same span makes it 3*8/4 = 6.0, so it is allocated FIRST, takes $v0, and the merged chain+dest quantity is forced onto $v1 - the target's seats with no group-A local, no schedule change and the D stores untouched.
frontier.mechanism: qty_compare_1 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/local-alloc.c:1660) ranks floor_log2(refs)*refs*size/(death-birth); flow.c accumulates reg_n_refs weighted by loop depth, so the reload pseudo currently scores 2 references x weight 2 = 4. Its span is pinned at 4 by the lw/sll/addu emission order (the target's own order), so refs is the only free term; two more references to the same pseudo, or one reference inside the inner do-while where the loop weight is higher, is the whole requirement.
frontier.next_probe: Start from tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s36/v/w3.c (27). Sweep spellings that reference the named reload local `q`'s SOURCE pseudo more often without adding an insn: the reload read into a local that also supplies the sb address, the reload local re-read inside the inner do-while for one of the two record pointers, and the reload named in a local whose second reference sits in the 0x5C/0x60 block while a separate read keeps that block's own lw. Check insns == 175 FIRST (any form that lets cse delete the second lw drops to 174), then qty-triage with s36/qty.sh for a reload quantity with refs >= 8 at span 4 before scoring.

frontier.hypothesis: x3's merged chain+dest quantity is already born at 12 without moving the D group, which is the birth s2/s4 had to displace the D stores to obtain. Re-running the s2/s4 store-group family on the x3 chassis may therefore pay for the seats twice and expose a body whose D stores sit at rows 52/53 with the address emitted at 49/50/51.
frontier.mechanism: s34/s35 established that the merged quantity's birth moves only when a store group is emitted ahead of the group-A stores; x3 shows a single-death group-A pointer moves it to 12 with no store reordering at all. The two levers have never been measured together, and the s2 residual (13 points, entirely the D group's emission position) is the smaller of the two residuals now on the table.
frontier.next_probe: Build x3 variants that additionally use s2's ptr-carried reload instead of the cast flip, and s4 variants that add the single-death group-A local, qty-triaging each with s36/qty.sh for four or five quantities with the merged chain+dest at birth <= 14 seated in $v1 and the reload in $v0, then score with s36/run.sh and row-diff against asm/funcs/func_800770B8.s to see which of rows 38-53 remain.
